The Joint Health Sector Union (JOHESU), Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) chapter, has issued a seven-day notice of industrial action to the FCT Administration over the failure to implement and pay arrears under the approved Professional Allowance Table (PAT).
The union comprises the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN) and the Nigerian Union of Allied Health Professionals (NUAHP).
The notice, jointly signed by the union chairman in FCT, Ene Nwachinerem, and the Secretary, Henry Oshowo, was made available to reporters in Abuja on Thursday.
The union said the notice was necessitated by the administration’s failure to pay the allowance to healthcare workers under the Consolidated Health Salary Structure (CONHESS).
According to the union, the notice will expire at midnight on 23 November, after which the union may embark on a full-scale strike if its demands remain unmet.
JOHESU recalled that it had earlier written to the FCTA on 7 August, through the office of the Head of Service, protesting what it described as a “discriminatory disparity in the implementation of the PAT”.
It said that while healthcare workers under the Consolidated Medical Salary Structure (CONMESS) benefited from the implementation, their counterparts under CONHESS were neglected.

“Regrettably, three months after the union formally submitted its complaint, drawing the attention of the FCT Administration to this unjustified dichotomy and demanding immediate implementation, no meaningful action has been taken,” it said.
“The union considers this continued delay unacceptable, discriminatory, and contrary to the principles of fairness, equity, and industrial harmony in the health sector.”
The union said the ultimatum followed repeated engagements with the administration and aligned with its national body’s directive.
It appealed to the Minister of the FCT, Nyesom Wike, to urgently intervene by directing the immediate implementation of the PAT for all eligible CONHESS staff and the settlement of all accruing arrears.
While reiterating its commitment to constructive engagement, JOHESU warned that industrial peace could not be sustained under prolonged neglect and unequal treatment.
“We wish to make it unequivocally clear that JOHESU FCTA cannot guarantee continued industrial harmony beyond the expiration of this seven-day notice if the outstanding issues are not satisfactorily addressed.
“Our members are therefore being prepared for the next line of action in accordance with the directives of the union,” it added.
